title: Nomura, Daiwa CEOs Flag Risk AI May Spoil Stock Market Rally
source_used: The Japan Times (same headline as the Bloomberg report)
key_facts: Nomura Holdings CEO Kentaro Okuda and Daiwa Securities Group CEO Akihiko Ogino spoke on a panel at a Nikkei event in Tokyo on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
Both expect Japan's stock rally to extend well into 2027, with a reversal in AI investment the main threat.
Okuda: 'If sentiment toward AI were to shift and that trend went into reverse, I think that could pose a significant risk.'
Ogino expects the Nikkei 225 at 80,000 this year and 88,000 toward the end of 2027; Okuda at about 75,000 by year-end and above 80,000 by end-2027. The gauge closed at 69,042.11 on Thursday.
Both pointed to the possibility that public opposition to AI and data centres in countries such as the US would reduce investment.
Ogino: market participants 'can change their views dramatically over a very short period of time'.
quote_evidence: “Markets, stock prices and corporate earnings are all being driven very strongly by investment in AI,” Nomura Holdings CEO Kentaro Okuda said at a Nikkei event in Tokyo on Thursday.
The gauge closed at 69,042.11 on Thursday.
Both executives pointed to the possibility that recent public opposition to AI and data centers in countries including the U.S. would lead to a drop in investment in the sector.
why_it_matters_hint: Heads of Japan's two largest brokerages say the stock rally depends heavily on AI investment sentiment.
